The cover has no other decoration. The scene of this frame is a wall calendar in a workshop office with eight days crossed through across its upper part and a ninth ringed further down the sheet. This frame is documentary: it is made on the real territory and the attached photographs govern every surface in it. Composition: a cut out subject on a warm white #F5F1E8 field with two flat duplicates of its own silhouette offset behind it on one axis, the first solid amber #E8A400, the second further out in graphite #14171C at low opacity. Edges stay hard, so it reads as risograph misregistration and not as blur. An amber beacon arc curves from the right edge into the depth, two white headlight lines sweep left to right and bend around an obstacle, the movers themselves gone or ghosted, while structure, edges and rails stay perfectly sharp. Camera 1.6 m high, 20 mm, f/11, ISO 100, 22 s. Ambient is mixed and deliberately uncorrected: 2000 K sodium on the far wall, 4000 K LED overhead, cold 6500 K spill from one opening. This is a working industrial park in the south of Moscow as it stands today, not an architectural visualisation: long low production blocks of pale warm grey concrete, two continuous ribbon bands of glazing in dark frames along each block, scaffolding on the part of the facade being renewed, roller shutter gates flush in the wall at yard level, a wide concrete apron with box trucks and semi trailers, lamp posts and standing water after rain. An office or conference hall is the renovated administrative building: white walls with one amber accent wall, black framed glazed partitions, grey carpet, linear ceiling light. Photoreal and physically correct, at the level of a high end render married to a documentary photograph: true reflections and roughness on every material, believable contact shadows, caustics on wet concrete, subsurface glow through a lit edge. Letters have real physical depth and catch the key light on their lit edge. The headline is laid flat on the ground plane in perspective, thin uppercase in warm white #F5F1E8, with one light trail passing in front of it, so the long exposure happened on top of the type. The brand mark sits flat on the same ground plane beside the headline, about three percent of the frame width, foreshortened by the same perspective.
